title: Content Moderation Pipeline
summary: A moderation pipeline screens a huge volume of uploads against a platform's rules. Known illegal material is caught by matching hashes against shared databases, and ML classifiers score everything else for policy categories. Clear cases are actioned automatically, uncertain ones go to trained human reviewers prioritised by severity and reach. Every decision can be appealed, and outcomes become training labels.

walkthrough.title: Content is uploaded
walkthrough.text: A user posts an image with a caption. It is stored and queued for screening; high-risk surfaces like live video and new accounts are screened before the post goes public.

walkthrough.title: Match known-bad hashes
walkthrough.text: A perceptual hash (PDQ, PhotoDNA) is compared against industry databases of known child-abuse and terrorist content. Perceptual hashes survive resizing and re-encoding, unlike exact checksums.

walkthrough.title: Score with classifiers
walkthrough.text: Image, text, and video models score each policy category: nudity, violence, hate speech, spam, self-harm. Each score is a probability, not a verdict.

walkthrough.title: Decide automatically
walkthrough.text: The policy engine applies per-category thresholds. A hash match or very high score means remove; very low means allow; borderline cases may be shown with reduced distribution while they wait.

walkthrough.title: Queue for human review
walkthrough.text: Uncertain items join review queues ordered by severity times expected views, so a borderline post going viral is seen before an obscure one.

walkthrough.title: Enforce and notify
walkthrough.text: The verdict is applied: remove, age-gate, label, or strike the account. The user is told which rule was broken and how to appeal.

walkthrough.title: Appeals and retraining
walkthrough.text: Appeals go to a different reviewer. Overturned decisions and fresh reviewer labels feed back into classifier training and threshold tuning.

data.label: User Uploads
responsibilities: Submit content along with context: surface, audience, author history.
Let users report content, which is an extra signal.
Show users clear notices and appeal options.

failureModes.mitigation: OCR and multimodal models; regular red-teaming against new evasion tricks.
Weight reports by reporter reliability; reports prioritise review but never decide alone.

data.label: Moderation Orchestrator

output.name: Signals
output.type: Hash matches + classifier scores bundled for decision

responsibilities: Fans each item out to the hash and classifier services in parallel.
Chooses blocking (pre-publish) or async screening by risk.
Re-screens content when models or policies change.

failureModes.scenario: Screening backlog during a viral event
failureModes.impact: Harmful content stays up for hours.
failureModes.mitigation: Prioritise by reach; autoscale; temporarily tighten thresholds on hot topics.

failureModes.impact: Either nothing posts, or nothing is screened.
failureModes.mitigation: Per-surface fail mode: hold live video, publish text and re-screen later.

data.label: Hash Matching
responsibilities: Detects re-uploads of known violating media with near-zero false positives.
Shares new hashes with other platforms through industry programmes.
Handles legally required reporting (e.g. to NCMEC) for matched content.

failureModes.impact: Hash distance too large to match.
failureModes.mitigation: Multiple hash types, matching on video segments, and classifier backup.

failureModes.scenario: Bad hash added to a bank
failureModes.mitigation: Review before banking and monitoring of appeal overturns per hash.

data.label: ML Classifiers
responsibilities: Scores new, unseen content for each policy category.
Supports many languages and regions, with cultural context.
Is retrained regularly on reviewer labels and appeal outcomes.

failureModes.mitigation: Fairness evaluation per language and group; calibrated thresholds; diverse labellers.
Route context-dependent categories to humans rather than auto-action.

data.label: Policy Decision Engine

input.name: Signals
input.type: Hash matches, scores, reports, author history

responsibilities: Turns scores into actions using thresholds set by policy teams.
Sends uncertain or high-impact cases to humans.
Logs the reason behind every automated action.

failureModes.impact: Mass false removals and a public backlash.
failureModes.mitigation: Shadow-test thresholds; watch appeal overturn rates per category.

failureModes.impact: Queues explode and SLAs are missed.

data.label: Human Review Queues

input.name: Case
input.type: Content + context + model hints, priority score

responsibilities: Trained reviewers judge nuanced cases against detailed guidelines.
Routes cases by language, region, and specialism (e.g. child safety).
Measures reviewer accuracy with audited golden sets.

failureModes.mitigation: Blurring and greyscale by default, exposure limits, wellness support.
Clear guidelines, calibration sessions, and double review for high impact.

data.label: Enforcement & Appeals

output.name: Effects
output.type: Takedown, strikes, notices; labels for training

responsibilities: Applies actions and tracks account strikes over time.
Notifies users with the specific rule and an appeal path.
Feeds appeal outcomes and labels back to model training.

failureModes.impact: Mistakes stand and users lose trust; may break laws such as the EU DSA.
failureModes.mitigation: Appeals reviewed by a different person; transparency reports.

failureModes.impact: New accounts reupload the same content.
failureModes.mitigation: Ban-evasion signals (device, payment, network) and hash-banking removed media.
